source: Flexiple GCC statistics: State GCC policies in India
note: Four states have published a GCC policy or scheme Flexiple could source to an official page or the policy document itself.

verified.policy: Karnataka Global Capability Centres Policy 2024 to 2029
verified.summary: Targets 500 new capability centres, taking the state past 1,000 by 2029, with 350,000 new jobs and $50 billion of economic output. Incentive bands include a Beyond Bengaluru tier for centres set up outside the capital.
verified.originalSource: Government of Karnataka and India Briefing

verified.policy: Gujarat Global Capability Centre Policy 2025 to 2030
verified.summary: Targets a minimum of 250 new GCC units, more than 50,000 jobs and Rs 10,000 crore of investment in the state.
verified.originalSource: Department of Science and Technology, Government of Gujarat

verified.summary: Targets around 400 new GCCs and about 400,000 high skilled jobs by 2030 against Rs 50,600 crore of investment, with incentives to push centres to Nagpur, Nashik and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.
verified.eligibilityNote: Incentives favour centres outside Mumbai and Pune.

verified.policy: Special scheme to promote global capability centres
verified.summary: A payroll subsidy scheme announced in the 2024 to 2025 state budget, running to March 2027, aimed at bringing 50 GCCs to the state.
verified.eligibilityNote: Limited to Forbes Global 2000 and Fortune 1000 parents committing at least 200 direct jobs.
verified.originalSource: Government of Tamil Nadu, 2024 to 2025 budget

couldNotVerify: Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh GCC policies. No official policy document could be fetched for any of them.
